narrative.intro: National Government Services obligated $278M in federal contracts in FY2026 to date. National Government Services received 8 awards so far, with an average award size of $34.8M, and obligations are up 6.6% year over year. Yearly obligations show variability: FY21 was $256M, FY22 was $254M, FY23 was $285M, FY24 was $186M, FY25 was $261M, and FY26 is $278M. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers is the largest NAICS market for National Government Services with $204M in obligations in FY2026 to date, followed by Computer Systems Design Services with $64M and Other Computer Related Services with $10.3M. The figures reported are contract obligations except where noted that largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables would show total contract values. Current-year totals are partial because FY2026 is fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: How have obligations for National Government Services changed over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Obligations rose and fell across the period shown. National Government Services obligated $256M in FY21, $254M in FY22, $285M in FY23, $186M in FY24, $261M in FY25, and $278M in FY26 to date. FY26 obligations are up 6.6% year over year compared with the prior partial year. The FY24 figure was the low point at $186M.

sections.heading: What are National Government Services largest markets in FY2026 to date?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers is the largest industry for National Government Services with $204M in obligations. Computer Systems Design Services is the second-largest with $64M. Other Computer Related Services accounts for $10.3M.
